title: Opposite Schubert divisors form the degree-dual Picard basis
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and such that every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; central means commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq G$, where $B$ is a Borel subgroup. Use the character lattice $X^*(T)$, positive roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$, their coroots, and $p:B\to T$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Write $Q=G/B$ and $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$, choose representatives $n_w$, and use $w_0$ and the open cell $C=Un_{w_0}B/B$ of [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], where $U$ is the unipotent radical of $B$. Set $s_j=s_{\alpha_j}\in W$, the reflection of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] acting by $s_{\alpha_j}(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle\alpha_j$, and $R_j=\overline{Bn_{s_j}B/B}_{\mathrm{red}}\subseteq Q$. Put $B^-=n_{w_0}Bn_{w_0}^{-1}$ and $E_i=\overline{B^-n_{s_i}B/B}_{\mathrm{red}}$. Each $R_j$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_F$. The $E_i$ are nonempty reduced irreducible effective Cartier divisors, meaning their ideal sheaves are locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Their translates $D_i=n_{w_0}E_i$ have pairwise distinct supports, and these supports are precisely the irreducible components of $Q\setminus C$; in particular $Q\setminus C=\bigcup_i|D_i|$. Let $\operatorname{Pic}(Q)$ be the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_Q$-modules under tensor product. Degree on the curves has the meaning of [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. The map $$d:\operatorname{Pic}(Q)\longrightarrow\mathbf Z^r,\qquad [L]\longmapsto\bigl(\deg(L|_{R_j})\bigr)_{j=1}^r$$ is a group isomorphism and $$\deg\bigl(\mathcal O_Q(E_i)|_{R_j}\bigr)=\delta_{ij},$$ where $\mathcal O_Q(E_i)=\mathcal I_{E_i}^{\vee}$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. These assertions hold in every characteristic; for the trivial group all indexed families are empty and $\operatorname{Pic}(Q)=0$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] the semisimple group is reductive. Hence [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry] makes $Q$ smooth projective, and [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts] makes it integral with affine-space charts and longest cell $C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] it is regular and locally Noetherian; its finite affine-space cover makes it Noetherian. It is separated (proper over $F$, with affine base $\operatorname{Spec}F$). Thus the regular Noetherian separated scheme case of [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] applies. The rank-one maps in [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-schubert-curve-degree] identify every $R_j$ with $\mathbf P^1_F$.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.62--63, and Exercise 2.2.E(2), printed pp.70--71 (all characteristics); expanded argument by Q44.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-schubert-closure-cell-geometry]. Each $E_i=X^-_{s_i}$ is integral of dimension $N-1$. Every nonidentity $x\in W$ has a simple reflection in a reduced word, so $s_i\leq x$ for some $i$; the opposite closure formula gives $Q\setminus C^-_1=\bigcup_i|E_i|$. If $s_i\leq s_j$ then $i=j$ by the length inequality; hence $e_{s_j}$ lies only in $E_j$, so these components are distinct and none contains another. They are precisely the irreducible components of that complement. At a point of $E_i$ its integral codimension-one ideal is a height-one prime in a regular local ring. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] (empty parameter family), that ring is a UFD; thus the prime is generated by a prime element, a nonzerodivisor. Consequently the reduced closed subscheme $E_i$ is an effective Cartier divisor.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.62--63, and Exercise 2.2.E(2), printed pp.70--71 (all characteristics); expanded argument by Q44.

proof.text: Left multiplication by $n_0=n_{w_0}$ is an automorphism of $Q$. By [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], $w_0^2=1$, so $n_0^2\in T$. Directly $n_0C=B^-n_0^2B/B=C^-_1$ and $n_0C^-_1=C$; the latter uses that $n_0^2\in T$ preserves $C$. Therefore it carries exactly the components $|E_i|$ of the opposite boundary to the distinct components $|D_i|$ of $Q\setminus C$. This proves the asserted boundary description without identifying divisor classes of translates.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.62--63, and Exercise 2.2.E(2), printed pp.70--71 (all characteristics); expanded argument by Q44.

proof.text: Fix $i,j$. The closure formula of [lem-sfb-schubert-closure-cell-geometry] excludes $e_1$ from $E_i$, and puts $e_{s_j}$ in $E_i$ exactly for $i=j$. The rank-one map of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-schubert-curve-degree] is equivariant for the diagonal torus via $\alpha_j^\vee$; on the first-column model $\mathbf P^1$ this acts as $[a:b]\mapsto[t a:t^{-1}b]$. The two endpoints are $e_1,e_{s_j}$, and every other geometric orbit is their complement: every nonzero scalar has a square root over an algebraically closed field, even in characteristic two. The closed invariant intersection $|E_i|\cap|R_j|$ cannot meet this orbit, since its closure contains $e_1$. Its support is thus empty for $i\ne j$ and the single rational point $e_{s_j}$ for $i=j$.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.62--63, and Exercise 2.2.E(2), printed pp.70--71 (all characteristics); expanded argument by Q44.

proof.text: For $i=j$, the opposite cell $C^-_{s_j}$ is open in $E_j$, and $C_{s_j}$ is open in $R_j$. By [lem-sfb-schubert-closure-cell-geometry] their tangent spaces at $e_{s_j}$ are complementary, with dimensions $N-1$ and $1$. If $f$ is a local equation of $E_j$, its differential is therefore nonzero on $T_{e_{s_j}}R_j$: the smooth hypersurface $E_j$ has tangent kernel $df$. The image of $f$ in the regular local ring of the smooth curve $R_j$ lies in $\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$, so it generates $\mathfrak m$ by Nakayama. Thus the restricted Cartier divisor is the reduced point $[e_{s_j}]$, with multiplicity one. For $i\ne j$ the restriction is empty. Locally restricting $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Q$ identifies the restricted line bundle with the line of this divisor. By [lem-pc-degree-agrees-sc], its degree is respectively $1$ or $0$.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.62--63, and Exercise 2.2.E(2), printed pp.70--71 (all characteristics); expanded argument by Q44.

proof.text: Put $O=C^-_1=n_0C\simeq\mathbf A_F^N$. By [lem-sfb-affine-space-invertible-trivial], every invertible $L$ is trivial on $O$. Choose such a trivialization and view its generator as a rational section $s$ on integral $Q$. The dictionary [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] associates the finite Weil divisor $\operatorname{div}(s)$ and identifies $L$ with $\mathcal O_Q(\operatorname{div}(s))$. Its coefficients vanish at codimension-one points in $O$, because $s$ generates there. The remaining codimension-one subvarieties are exactly $E_i$, so $\operatorname{div}(s)=\sum_i a_i E_i$ for integers $a_i$. Locally the fractional ideals for sums multiply, $f^{-1}\mathcal O\otimes g^{-1}\mathcal O\simeq(fg)^{-1}\mathcal O$; hence $[L]=\sum_i a_i[\mathcal O_Q(E_i)]$. This proves generation, not merely existence of some effective generators.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.62--63, and Exercise 2.2.E(2), printed pp.70--71 (all characteristics); expanded argument by Q44.

proof.text: The degree homomorphism of [def-sc-pic0] agrees on every line bundle on each smooth proper $R_j$ with the Euler-characteristic degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]: subtract the structure-sheaf case from the line-bundle formula in [lem-sc-riemann-roch]. Consequently $d$ is a group homomorphism. Step 5 sends $[\mathcal O_Q(E_i)]$ to the $i$th standard vector. Step 6 expresses every class as a sum of these classes; taking degrees recovers each coefficient $a_j$. Therefore $a\mapsto\sum_i a_i[\mathcal O_Q(E_i)]$ is a two-sided inverse to $d$, proving the stated isomorphism and dual basis. When the families are empty, the opposite cell is all of $Q$, and Step 6 gives $[L]=0$ for every $L$; all assertions, including the trivial group case, follow.
